answer: A farm running 143 keys therefore pays that exposure on every endorsement it manufactures, which removes the asymmetry that normally makes mass attestation low-cost. Because the kernel stake is held until the cedar settlement, the operator carries real capital per endorsement, and the ivory audit lists each exposure. An attester must stake 24% of the reward its attestation would unlock, so endorsing a high-value answer costs proportionally more than endorsing a trivial one. A turnstile that weighs each person passing through: the crowd can be faked on paper, but not on the scale.
